Topics · Is the Quran from God?

Why believe a miracle story from long ago?

Hume objects strongly. Yet the Quran quotes the demand for wonders and does not build on them. So on what?

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَقَالُوا۟ لَوْلَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَيْهِ ءَايَـٰتٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦ ۖ قُلْ إِنَّمَا ٱلْـَٔايَـٰتُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَإِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ٥٠ أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِهِمْ أَنَّآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَرَحْمَةً وَذِكْرَىٰ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ٥١﴾

Translation of the meaning

But they say, "Why are not signs sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "The signs are only with Allāh, and I am only a clear warner." And is it not sufficient for them that We revealed to you the Book [i.e., the Qur’ān] which is recited to them? Indeed in that is a mercy and reminder for a people who believe.

Quran · Al-Ankabut 29:50-51

Hume's point deserves its full weight. Reports of wonders come from long ago, through retelling, and every tradition has them. Doubting them is reasonable. Here is what is unusual: the Quran quotes that demand, and it does not answer with a wonder. People ask for signs. The reply is that signs are with God, and that the speaker is only a warner. Then it asks whether the recitation itself is not enough. It declines to rest its case where Hume attacks.

A question for you

What would you have asked for, if you had been in that crowd?

If you sayA clear wonder, with my own eyes.
ThenThat is an understandable request, and the text itself records it. It comes next.
If you sayAn argument, not a wonder.
ThenThen you agree with the text's stance here, and it has to deliver.
If you sayNothing would convince me.
ThenThat is honest. It is worth asking whether that is a view about evidence, or about the subject as a whole.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَقَالُوا۟ لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ تَفْجُرَ لَنَا مِنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ يَنۢبُوعًا٩٠ أَوْ تَكُونَ لَكَ جَنَّةٌ مِّن نَّخِيلٍ وَعِنَبٍ فَتُفَجِّرَ ٱلْأَنْهَـٰرَ خِلَـٰلَهَا تَفْجِيرًا٩١ أَوْ تُسْقِطَ ٱلسَّمَآءَ كَمَا زَعَمْتَ عَلَيْنَا كِسَفًا أَوْ تَأْتِىَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ قَبِيلًا٩٢ أَوْ يَكُونَ لَكَ بَيْتٌ مِّن زُخْرُفٍ أَوْ تَرْقَىٰ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَلَن نُّؤْمِنَ لِرُقِيِّكَ حَتَّىٰ تُنَزِّلَ عَلَيْنَا كِتَـٰبًا نَّقْرَؤُهُۥ ۗ قُلْ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّى هَلْ كُنتُ إِلَّا بَشَرًا رَّسُولًا٩٣﴾

Translation of the meaning

And they say, "We will not believe you until you break open for us from the ground a spring Or [until] you have a garden of palm trees and grapes and make rivers gush forth within them in force [and abundance] Or you make the heaven fall upon us in fragments as you have claimed or you bring Allāh and the angels before [us] Or you have a house of ornament [i.e., gold] or you ascend into the sky. And [even then], we will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book we may read." Say, "Exalted is my Lord! Was I ever but a human messenger?"

Quran · Al-Isra 17:90-93

Look at the list of demands in this passage: a spring from the ground, a garden, the sky falling in pieces, God and angels brought before us, a house of gold, a climb into the sky, a book to read. It sounds like every sceptic in history. The reply to all of it is short: glory to my Lord; am I anything but a human messenger? So the man himself declines the role of wonder-worker. Whatever else you think, the text does not present him that way.

A question for you

What does it show that a man refuses this role?

If you sayHe couldn't, which is natural.
ThenThat is a possible and simple explanation, and it stands with what he said of himself.
If you sayRare honesty for someone claiming prophecy.
ThenA piece of evidence, no more. You decide its weight.
If you sayIt shows nothing.
ThenThat is your view. The main argument does not lie here.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَمَا مَنَعَنَآ أَن نُّرْسِلَ بِٱلْـَٔايَـٰتِ إِلَّآ أَن كَذَّبَ بِهَا ٱلْأَوَّلُونَ ۚ وَءَاتَيْنَا ثَمُودَ ٱلنَّاقَةَ مُبْصِرَةً فَظَلَمُوا۟ بِهَا ۚ وَمَا نُرْسِلُ بِٱلْـَٔايَـٰتِ إِلَّا تَخْوِيفًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And nothing has prevented Us from sending signs [i.e., miracles] except that the former peoples denied them. And We gave Thamūd the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her. And We send not the signs except as a warning.

Quran · Al-Isra 17:59

So why does a wonder not settle things? This sentence gives one reason: earlier peoples saw signs and denied them. A wonder does not create trust where there is none; it only makes the argument about the wonder. So the Quran turns to what anyone can inspect now: the world, the self, the text. If that is weak, it is weak in the open. This is not proof. It means you can judge the case today, with no witness from the past.

A question for you

Where would you rather begin to examine things?

If you sayWith the world: why is there anything?
ThenThat question needs no witness from the past.
If you sayWith the text itself.
ThenThen let us look at how it can be tested.
If you sayWith the man who brought it.
ThenThat is a serious question, and it has its Step.

Your reflection

What is the strangest thing that has happened to you, which you could not make anyone believe?
